chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Jumhur, from his father, who raised it (as marfu'), from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) frequently used to say: 'Know with certain knowledge that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not made it possible for the servant — even if his striving is intense, his resourcefulness great, and his endurance abundant — to surpass what has been decreed for him in the Wise Remembrance; nor has He prevented the servant, in his weakness and scarcity of means, from reaching what has been named for him in the Wise Remembrance.

O people! No one gains even a fraction by his cleverness, and no one loses even a fraction by his foolishness. So the one who knows this and acts accordingly is the most at ease among people in his benefit, and the one who knows this yet abandons it is the most burdened among people in his loss. How often one who is blessed is being gradually lured astray through those blessings, and how often one who appears deceived among the people is actually being cared for.

So come to your senses, O you who strive, from your striving; restrain your haste; awaken from the slumber of your heedlessness; and reflect upon what has come from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, upon the tongue of His Prophet (may Allah bless him and his family). And preserve these seven letters, for they are from the words of the People of Wisdom and from the firm decrees of Allah in the Wise Remembrance.

That no one should meet Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with any of these traits — associating partners with Allah in what He has made obligatory upon him; venting rage at the cost of his own destruction; approving of a matter that another commits; seeking to gain favor with a creature by manifesting an innovation in his religion; being pleased that people praise him for what he has not done; the arrogant and conceited; or the one possessing pomp and pride.

O people! The predators, their ambition is transgression; the animals, their ambition is their bellies; the women, their ambition is men; and the believers — they are compassionate, fearful, and trembling. May Allah make us and you among them.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْحِجَى: The People of Reason/Understanding — referring to the Imams (AS) and their tradition of wisdom
key_terms.الذِّكْرِ الْحَكِيمِ: The Wise Remembrance — a Quranic epithet referring to the Quran (cf. 36:2); here used to indicate that provisions are written in divine decree
key_terms.الْحُرُوفُ السَّبْعَة: The seven letters — the seven moral vices enumerated in the hadith that one must not bring to God
key_terms.عَزَائِم اللَّهِ: The firm/resolved decrees of Allah — matters that admit no exception
key_terms.نَقِير: A tiny notch on a date-stone — proverbial for the most infinitesimal amount

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about divine providence and the futility of excessive striving for livelihood?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a sermon that Imam Ali (AS) frequently delivered, addressing the fundamental Islamic doctrine of divine providence in sustenance (rizq). Imam Ali (AS) taught that no degree of human effort can cause one to exceed or fall short of what God has decreed — this knowledge should bring peace rather than anxiety. The sermon then articulates seven moral vices that would cause one to meet God in a state of spiritual ruin, culminating with a powerful contrast between the base drives of animals and the God-consciousness of true believers.
word_analysis: a fraction (lit. notch of a date-stone)

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Jamhour, from his father, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘What Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> frequently used to say was: ‘Know with a knowledge of certainty that Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic did not Make for the servant, even if his striving was intense and his means were great and his planning was a lot, that he should preceed what is Named for him in the Wise Remembrance, and did not Loosen from the servant in his weakness and the scarcity of his planning that he should reach what is Named for him in the Wise Remembrance. 
O you people! It (livelihood) will not increase a person with a fraction due to his cleverness and would not reduce a person a fraction due to his stupidity. So the one who knows this and works by it would be the greatest of the people in rest with regards to his profits, and the one who knows this and is a neglector of it would be the busiest of the people in his losses; and sometimes he would be allured towards it with the goodness to it, and sometimes he would be deceived among the people, dealing for it. 
So be (persistant) with your striving, O you striver, and reduce from your haste and become aware from your oblivion (forgetfulness), and ponder regarding what has come from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic upon the tongue of His<sup>azwj</sup> Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and preserve these seven letter, for these are from the words of the People<sup>asws</sup> of the Proofs, and from the Resoved issues of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in the Wise Remembrance (Holy Quran). 
It is not for anyone that he should meet Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic with a characteristic from these characterists – Association (Shirk) with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> in whatever Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Necessitated upon him, or healing an anger destroying himself, or accepting with a matter which others have done, or perform for the people by manifesting an innovation in his Religion, or be joyful if the people were to praise him with what he has not done, and the swaggering of the tyrants, or the ones with the pomp and the pride. 
O you people! The predators, their incination is towards the aggression; and the beasts, their inclination is towards their bellies; and the women, their inclination is towards the men; and the Believers, they are cautious, fearful, afraid. May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make us<sup>asws</sup> and you all, to be from them’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from ibn Jumhur from his father in a marfu’ manner who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, very often would say, ‘You must take notice with absolute certainty that Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, does not allow a servant, no matter how intensely he strives, how great the kind of means he prepares, and no matter how numerously he suffers fatigue, to exceed the limit which He has mentioned in His book of wisdom. It does not change anything for a man, with his weakness and his little means, in reaching what is already assigned for him in the book of wisdom.

O people, one’s wisdom does not increase a naqir (a certain unit of measurement) for him and one’s lack of understanding does not reduce anything against him. One who knows this and acts accordingly is the greatest of people to enjoy comfort in profit, and one who knows it but ignores to act accordingly does the biggest work to cause losses. There are many of those who are led to destruction in the process of receiving favors, and also there are many of those who are thought of among people as being deceived, but in reality receive favors.

O you who strive hard, beware of your struggle, hold back your haste and wake up from the slumber of your unawareness. Think about what has come from Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, through the tongue of His Holy prophet. Preserve these seven letters; they are of the words of the people of reason and of the decisive issues in the book of wisdom.

One cannot reach before Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, with the presence of any single of these habits in him: considering things as partners of Allah in the matters that Allah has made obligatory on him, quenching his anger by destruction of his soul, claiming to have done what in fact others have done, seeking success before a creature by means of a heretic act in his religion, enjoying people’s praising him for what he has not done, acting oppressively and conceitedly, and being of honorable position but speaking lies.

O people, what is important for beasts is transgression, and what is important for animals is to eat, what is important for women is their men; and believing people are anxious, fearful and afraid. I pray to Allah to make us one of them (such believers).”’
